did_you_know.text: Did you know? Job describes his complaint as bitter and painful, saying that his hand is heavy because of his groaning.
Did you know? Job longs to know where he can find God and reach His dwelling place, so he can present his case before Him.
Did you know? Job compares meeting God to a court hearing: he wants to present his case before Him and fill his mouth with arguments.
Did you know? Job asks whether God would contend with him using great power, suggesting that he hopes the judgment will be based on fairness rather than merely a display of strength.
Did you know? Job searches for God in every direction—forward, backward, to the left, and to the right—but cannot see Him or understand where He is.
Did you know? Although Job cannot find God, he says that God knows his way, and he expresses confidence that after being tested, he will come out pure as gold.
Did you know? Job declares that he has followed God's way, kept to it, and not turned aside from it.
Did you know? Job says that he has not departed from God's commands, and that he has treasured and kept the words of His mouth in his heart.
Did you know? Job describes God as one who acts according to His own will, and no one can turn Him back or prevent Him from doing whatever He desires.
Did you know? Recognizing God's power causes Job to be terrified and afraid; he describes his heart as growing weak before Him.
